raw.details:
About Hack the Fork:

Hack the Fork NIFTEM-K is an AI × Alternative Protein hackathon organised by Hack the Fork, a France-based non-profit, in collaboration with NIFTEM, bringing together students, innovators, researchers, food-tech enthusiasts, and AI builders to explore how artificial intelligence can help shape the future of food.

Participants will work on real-world challenges at the intersection of AI, food technology, sustainability, and alternative proteins, and develop innovative solutions with the potential to create meaningful impact.

Why Participate:

  • Solve real-world challenges at the intersection of AI and food innovation.
  • Learn about the rapidly evolving alternative protein ecosystem.
  • Work with an interdisciplinary team.
  • Get mentorship from experts.
  • Build and showcase an innovative solution.
  • Network with students, researchers, entrepreneurs, and industry professionals.
  • Compete for exciting prizes/recognition.
  • Receive certificates.

Eligibility Criteria:

  • Applicants must apply in teams of 2–5 members.
  • All members are currently pursuing a UG/PG/Doctoral or other program at a registered institute.
  • Teams can be formed from different universities/colleges.
  • Teams are encouraged to be from multiple disciplines (but not required).
  • All members would be able to attend the Hackathon on the offline dates if selected.

Instructions for Applicants:

  • One submission per team. The form must be filled by the team leader.
  • Teams must have 2 to 5 members. All members must be currently enrolled undergraduate or postgraduate students.
  • Cross-institution teams are allowed and encouraged. Interdisciplinary teams are strongly preferred.
  • You do not need a working prototype to apply. You need a clear problem and a credible plan.
  • The Top 20 teams will be invited to NIFTEM-K, Kundli, for the 24-hour build on 24 and 25 October 2026. Arrival is on the evening of 23 October.
  • Accommodation and all meals are provided for selected teams. All catering is 100% plant-based.
  • Teams travelling from more than 50 km away can arrive on 23 October from 4 PM.
  • Teams pay for their own travel to and from NIFTEM-K, Kundli.

Themes:

Plant-Based:

AI for formulation and indigenous crops.

Scope: Texture, nutrition, and sensory prediction. Reformulation from underutilized Indian raw material and crop side streams.

Fermentation:

AI for bioprocess and scale-up.

Scope: Yield prediction, digital twins for bioreactors, cutting batch failure in fermentation-derived protein, and simplifying scale-up.

Open:

AI across Food Systems.

Scope: Open to all AI solutions across the food system. Supply chain, food safety, nutrition, food waste, and consumer insights.
